title: I absolutely hate that they did this- something to be aware of if you...
transcript: Can I just complain for a second about the way that they have handled the wicked for good soundtracks? I may be late to the party here, but I haven't really seen anyone else discussing this and it really bothers me. You may have already noticed this if you have listened to the soundtrack on Spotify or if you bought a vinyl or the CD yourself, but the official soundtrack of wicked for good does not include the finale. This is not a huge issue if you listen to your music digitally, as they have released the finale as a single. But if you like physical media, the only way to listen to the finale is by buying a completely different vinyl or CD. That being the wicked for good score album, which contains all of the instrumental music used in the movie. It also, for reasons that can only be described as greed, contains the finale, which is the only track on that album that contains vocals. And I say it's greedy because there is absolutely no reason that the finale needs to be on that score album and not on the regular soundtrack album. If you compare it to the first wicked album, that album had 12 songs and a run time of 56 minutes. This album has 11 songs and a run time of 44 minutes. That means you could easily fit the finale on here and still have the same number of songs as the first Album and be eight minutes shorter. The only reason to not include the family on here is to essentially trick people into buying the score album that probably were not going to buy the score album. It is just an incredibly anti consumer practice. And honestly, had I known that when I bought this album, I probably would not have bought this album. I'm totally fine with wicked getting their bag, and if they wanna release 100 different final variants, they're welcome to do that, but at least release a complete album before you make a hundred different versions of it.
classificationReason: Complaint about how the Wicked for Good movie soundtrack was released across physical media formats — not about the stage production.
